# Elessar

> Open-source Python library for exploratory data analysis and statistical profiling, distributed under the MIT licence. Requires Python 3.10 or later.

Elessar produces documented statistical assessments and HTML reports. Its scope includes data quality, distributions, associations, multivariate analysis and exploratory feature selection. Statistical findings depend on data and assumptions; diagnostics do not guarantee predictive performance or detect every instance of data leakage.

## Documentation
- [Complete guide](https://thibautdqb.github.io/elessar-site/guide.html): Features, methodology, installation, FAQ and roadmap. Readable without JavaScript.
- [Complete guide as Markdown](https://thibautdqb.github.io/elessar-site/content-english.md): Plain-text version of the English guide.
- [Full text reference](https://thibautdqb.github.io/elessar-site/llms-full.txt): Complete guide in one text file.
- [Presentation](https://thibautdqb.github.io/elessar-site/): Interactive visual introduction.

## Authoritative project sources
- [Source and technical documentation](https://github.com/Thibautdqb/elessar)
- [Package and published versions](https://pypi.org/project/elessar/)
- [Release notes](https://github.com/Thibautdqb/elessar/releases)

## Usage
Install with `pip install elessar`. Example: `import elessar; report = elessar.see("data.csv")`.

## Version accuracy
The guide describes version 1.2 as in preparation. Verify current availability, API and version-specific features against PyPI and official release notes. Roadmap items are not released features. The website is a presentation of the Python library; it does not run analyses on uploaded data.
